The Affordable Innovation for the Grid Act, would direct the Department of Energy, FERC, and IRC to analyze how high-performance computing and AI can enhance our bulk power system and assess what limitations may delay their adoption. As energy demand continues to grow at a lightning pace, grid infrastructure needs to operate at peak efficiency and capacity. These emerging technologies have the potential to provide our grid operators with the tools to dramatically speed up the interconnection queue process, expediting timelines to bring new generation online. They can also enhance existing operations through predictive maintenance—identifying what assets need repairs now, before they fail.

statements.text: I have heard from several stakeholders, including TVA and MISO, PJM, that AI and advanced computing tools can be one of the keys to enhance grid capacity operations and reliability. [...] And I have a bill called the Affordable Innovation for the Grid Act, which will help identify opportunities to enhance our grid through AI and find out what are the obstacles that are slowing down deployment.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Harshbarger at a House subcommittee hearing on AI and electrical grid capacity.

statements.text:
Interconnection studies are taking years when they should take months.

Today I introduced the Affordable Innovation for the Grid Act to assess how AI and High-Performance Computing can optimize our bulk-power system and cut through that backlog.

https://t.co/TYR1sjussd

America’s energy grid is the backbone of our economy, and we have an obligation to make sure it’s built for the future. Interconnection studies that should take months are taking years, and that backlog is a real drag on grid performance and American competitiveness. AI and High-Performance Computing can help us cut through that by optimizing how we operate existing infrastructure and getting more out of every line and generator. Right now, we don’t have a clear picture of where those technologies stand or what’s holding back wider adoption. This bill is a commonsense first step toward fixing that and making sure America leads the world in both energy and innovation.
statements.venue: Press release on introducing the Affordable Innovation for the Grid Act (with Rep. Mullin)
